Poetry Anthology: Love and Relationships / Conflict / Youth and Age
The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde

paper-1-exploring-modern-and-literary-he: A page from a novel you'll never read. Where do you even start?
paper-2-exploring-poetry-and-shakespeare: A poem you've never seen, twenty minutes. What do you look for first?
macbeth-themes: A brave hero in Act 1, a 'dead butcher' by Act 5. What went wrong?
an-inspector-calls: Why end the play with a phone call, not an arrest?
animal-farm: The farm ends with the name it started with. So what changed?
love--relationships-poetry: Her lover sails off to get rich for her. Why is she in tears?
poetry-anthology-love-and-relationships-: A children's poem about a rose-tree. Where is the conflict?
youth-and-age-poetry: Poor children sing in St Paul's. Is Blake cheering or warning?
unseen-poetry: A poem you've never seen, twenty minutes. What do you look for first?
romeo-and-juliet: The Prologue gives away the ending. Why would Shakespeare do that?
the-merchant-of-venice: Three weddings and a happy ending. So why do many audiences not laugh?
much-ado-about-nothing: Two love stories, one play. Why does Shakespeare need both?
the-strange-case-of-dr-jekyll-and-mr-hyd: Why does the novel hide its biggest secret until the last chapter?
a-christmas-carol: Why does Scrooge's whole life change in a single night?
great-expectations: Why does Dickens split Pip's life into three "stages"?
jane-eyre: Five homes, one girl. Why does Jane's story keep moving her on?
pride-and-prejudice: The novel's first line states a 'truth'. Should you believe it?
the-war-of-the-worlds: One man tells the story. How does he describe scenes he never saw?
